to.fees: $5/vehicle day-use e-Pass or $30 annual Northwest Forest Pass, purchasable via Recreation.gov
to.rules: Leave No Trace; no camping within 0.25 mile of Blue Lake; no stock or mechanized travel on the climbers' path
to.permit: No climbing or wilderness permit required
to.closures: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) is gated and closed for winter, typically early-to-mid December through mid-April/May depending on snowpack
to.seasonal: WA-20 (North Cascades Highway) closes gate-to-gate roughly early December–mid/late April; the entire Washington Pass corridor is car-inaccessible in winter.
to.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District
to.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
to.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
to.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency (America the Beautiful) Pass

overnight_permit.where: This is general Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest land outside any wilderness boundary; parties bivy informally at the trailhead or a highway pullout. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is needed to park, and no camping is allowed within a quarter mile of Blue Lake itself.
